title: STAT 110 Final: Probability and Grouped Data

allowance.rules: Student reports one sheet, both sides may be brought to the exam; paper size and content restrictions not supplied.

blocks.text: **Choose the reference group first.** P(A | B) = cases in both A and B / cases in B. The group after the bar is the denominator. P(A | B) and P(B | A) usually differ.

blocks.setup: One table; the question wording selects the denominator.

steps.label: Counts
steps.text: Among 25 commuters, 10 cycle and 15 do not. Among 15 noncommuters, 5 cycle and 10 do not. Totals: 30 cycle, 25 do not.

steps.label: Row percentage
steps.text: For commuter row: cycle 10/25 = 40.0%; do not cycle 15/25 = 60.0%. Row percentages use the row total; each row sums to 100%.

steps.label: Column percentage
steps.text: For cycle column: commuters 10/15 = 66.7%; noncommuters 5/15 = 33.3%. Column percentages use the column total; each column sums to 100%.

blocks.takeaway: Name the group the question asks about, then divide by that group's total. Always report the percentage and reference group.

blocks.prompt: A column percentage was requested, but the row total was selected.
blocks.first_error: The saved attempt selected the row total for a column percentage; the original question and reasoning are not in the record.
blocks.fix: For a column percentage, divide the cell by its column total. First name the reference group; it must match the requested column.
blocks.conditions: Row and column percentages each total 100% within their own reference group, not necessarily across the other direction.

blocks.text: **Reporting rule (outline):** every proportion as a percentage to 1 decimal place, with the reference group in words: “40.0% of commuters.”

Split cases by a categorical variable; compute one summary (such as a mean or count) per group. Output: one row per non-empty group, not one row per original case. Compare groups using the same summary (mean with mean, total with total).
